audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 against 52.81% over 784 games, and the page splits the lane correctly: Aurora owns levels 1-5 against an immobile enemy whose Flash Frost is a slow sphere on 11/10/9/8/7 costing up to 100 mana, then Anivia takes over from 6 when Glacial Storm can be held. Side lane and teamfights are hers because Crystallize is a flat 17s wall.

All four spikes are grounded: level 3-5 on Flash Frost's 11s whiff punishes, level 6 on the storm doubling Frostbite, first item on her mana stacking paying for a held storm, late on Crystallize cutting the exit plus Rebirth costing a second kill. The chart's flip at row 4 matches the packet levelChart exactly.

Both decisive interactions are already stated in Riot's own wording. Frostbite doubles its damage on a target recently hit by Flash Frost OR damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm — the page states both halves, and pairs it with Frostbite's flat 4s cooldown, which is why standing in the zone is the losing choice. Crystallize is an impassable wall that ends Across the Veil's leap, and Rebirth means the kill is not the kill until the egg breaks.

breakdown.cooldowns carries real digits and the right conclusion: Flash Frost 11s rank 1 to 7s rank 5, Crystallize flat 17s, Frostbite flat 4s — explicitly called out as the cooldown you cannot wait out.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why described her first item only as 'mana and health items' and then repeated generic zone language.
audit.why: The content layer already names the actual purchase (whys[5]: Rod of Ages/Liandry's), so the full layer should say the same thing and tie it to the mechanic that makes the item matter — a storm she can afford to hold, with Frostbite doubling off it every 4 seconds.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now names the item and the doubling cadence.

edits.before: She stacks mana and health items, and the storm covers the ground you wanted to fight on.
edits.after: Her Rod of Ages spike pays for a held storm; Frostbite doubles on a flat 4s inside it.

notes: Cleanest matchup in the slice. Level chart is fully consistent across all three layers — full-layer phases[].side, content win[], and the packet levelChart all read Aurora on rows 0-3 and Anivia on rows 4-6, and every why matches its verdict, so no chart edits were needed or made. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Flash Frost's' and 'Glacial Storm's' — both false positives, they are the correct Riot names with a possessive apostrophe. UNVERIFIED and deliberately not written: whether Crystallize's wall blocks Aurora's Q missile and E blast as well as movement. Riot's text says only 'block all movement', and the kit's terrain flag does not settle projectile behaviour, so no claim was made either way.
